dedupe_keys.name: magpie model of agricultural production and its impact on the environment

description: MAgPIE is an open-source global partial equilibrium model of the land-use sector from the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research. It runs in a recursive dynamic mode and brings spatially explicit biophysical constraints into economic decisions, to assess competition for land and water and the consequences for sustainable development under scenarios of food, energy and material demand, climate change impacts, greenhouse gas mitigation and land policies. Biophysical inputs such as crop yields, carbon densities and irrigation water availability come from the LPJmL model at 0.5 degree resolution. Land types are cropland (rainfed and irrigated, many crop groups and two second-generation bioenergy crops), pasture, forest, other land and settlements; production must meet demand for food, feed, seed, processing, bioenergy and materials, with trade based on historical patterns and competitiveness. The model is written in GAMS with R packages for pre- and post-processing. The latest release, 4.14.1 of 25 August 2026, is archived on Zenodo under AGPL-3.0-or-later, and the code is on GitHub. Caveats: it needs a GAMS licence with nonlinear solvers and large input data, and regions are aggregated for the economics. For simulation it projects land use, agricultural production and emissions for climate and food-system scenarios. Related catalogue records include GLOBIOM and GTAP.
